title: NEXY autonomous round 7 — canonical Next API transport binding
scope: DOC-C §4.1/§4.2 transport binding from Next UI routes to existing canonical API handlers
inputs_summary: Authoritative DOC-C route matrix, live Next app routes, API handler files, adapter semantics and GitHub Actions evidence.
actions: Proved UI used same-origin /api/* calls while apps/web/app/api contained no route bindings and next.config.js had no proxy/rewrites.
Added shared Next-to-legacy API adapter preserving body, params, cookies, headers, status, response headers and Express cookie maxAge semantics.
Bound implemented canonical auth/health/directive/run/freeze routes to existing handlers.
Audited route matrix and found non-canonical /api/auth/me drift; added canonical /api/session/me and removed the alias.
Kept unimplemented canonical API pack routes unbound rather than inventing backend behavior.
Ran complete CI on the final route-binding head.

claims_proofs.claim: Pre-R7 frontend API transport was absent.
claims_proofs.proof: No apps/web/app/api route files and no rewrite/proxy in apps/web/next.config.js while UI called /api/*.

claims_proofs.claim: Implemented canonical handlers are now reachable through same-origin Next routes.
claims_proofs.proof: Route files bind auth, session/me, directives, runs, freeze recovery and health handlers through the shared adapter.

claims_proofs.claim: R7 corrected a path-level spec drift rather than normalizing it.
claims_proofs.proof: DOC-C defines GET /api/session/me; non-canonical /api/auth/me route was removed and contract test now requires its absence.

claims_proofs.claim: R7 is regression-clean at the tested SHA.
claims_proofs.proof: Workflow 35554155180 passed module-boundary, full suite, contract, typecheck, migration, integration, DOC-C static gate and evidence attestation; deploy skipped.

successes: Same-origin Next transport exists for implemented canonical API handlers.
Canonical session route restored and non-canonical alias removed.
failures: Two local write attempts were aborted by branch drift before ref mutation because a concurrent execution chain had already advanced the same finding.
decisions: Do not invent missing canonical API handlers to satisfy current UI calls.
Treat DOC-C route matrix as build authority over comments/tests/UI aliases.
Keep server handlers on Node runtime.
unresolved: Canonical API pack still lacks POST /api/vault/commit, GET /api/artifacts/:id/revisions, GET /api/incidents/:id and GET /api/audit-logs.
Current UI contains non-canonical list calls /api/vault/artifacts, GET /api/directives, GET /api/runs and /api/audit.
Browser-level critical-flow E2E gate remains absent.
risks: Unimplemented canonical routes remain release blockers.
UI pages depending on non-canonical list endpoints still cannot be considered wired.
limits: R7 covers transport for existing handlers, not full canonical API-pack completeness.
rollback: Revert R7 route/adapter commits on the dedicated branch only if authoritative DOC-C route matrix changes; do not reintroduce /api/auth/me without spec extension.
next_actions: Implement missing canonical API pack routes with backend RBAC and audit semantics.
Then reconcile UI consumers to canonical routes or remove unsupported UI flows.
Add browser-level E2E gate after canonical API pack is complete.
